transcript: Sunday run before the week starts, legs feeling good these days, that base of training from the ten k still paying off. Sam and I are doing the low-key long-distance-relationship-with-a-day-job thing well I think, texted most of the morning. Getting the apartment squared away a bit before another Atlas week hits, dishes, some laundry, the usual Sunday reset.

Overcast Monday again, that same flat gray that seems to follow the start of every week this winter. Dragged myself through the morning, coffee doing the bare minimum. Nothing bad, just heavy in that low-grade way. Atlas still Atlas.

Awake at four again, mind spinning through Atlas blockers even though there is nothing to do about any of them at this hour. Thought this had gotten better in January but apparently not. Going to be a rough day running on this.

Tried something new today, actually told Priya I needed to push a nonessential meeting off my calendar to protect some focus time, first time I've really drawn a line like that since Atlas started. She was fine with it, more than fine actually, said she wished more people would do that. Small thing but it felt like a boundary worth practicing.

Pottery Thursday, wheel had other plans for me tonight, kept collapsing into a wobbling mess no matter what I tried. Frustrating after a couple weeks of actual progress, but the instructor reminded me that's just how it goes sometimes, the clay has moods too apparently. Still glad I came, even a bad pottery night beats sitting at home stewing about work.

Date night with Sam, easy and good as usual, tried a little Italian place near their apartment. Told them about the pottery disaster from last night and got properly laughed at, in the affectionate way. Things between us keep just steadily being good, no drama, which after a stretch of Atlas stress has been genuinely grounding.

Saturday run, longer one, and I noticed again how much this has become less about the ten k goal and more about just needing the reset, moving my body enough that my head goes quiet for forty-five minutes. Mood regulation more than fitness at this point, though the fitness is a nice side effect.

Mom called again tonight, and it wasn't good news exactly, more just an unsettled feeling underneath what she was saying. Nonna's had a rough couple of days, nothing acute, but Mom's voice had that thin quality to it, the one she gets when she's trying to protect me from how worried she actually is. Told her I love her, told her to call anytime, and hung up with this low unease sitting in my chest that hasn't quite lifted since.

Nonna died this morning. Mom called just after eight, and I knew before she even said the words, something in the half second of silence after I picked up. It was peaceful, apparently, in her sleep, which is the kind of detail people offer you like it's supposed to help and maybe it does a little, I don't know yet. I keep thinking about her kitchen, the yellow light in there in the afternoons, the way she'd say mangia, tesoro, eat, sweetheart, every single time food touched a table whether you were hungry or not, whether you were five or thirty five. Her hands, how they always smelled faintly of garlic and rosemary no matter how many times she washed them. I don't really know what to do with myself right now. I called out of work, told Priya just enough, she was kind about it, didn't push for details. I keep picking up my phone to text someone and then remembering there's nothing to text, there's just this, sitting in it. I don't have anything wise to say tonight. I just wanted to write down that she was here, and that she made a whole kitchen feel like being loved.

Went into work today because staying home alone with my own head felt worse than going in. Mostly just autopilot, answering emails without really reading them, nodding through a meeting I couldn't tell you a single detail of afterward. Nobody pushed, everyone was gentle about it in that careful way people are when they know something's happened but don't quite know how to ask. Numb mostly. That's the honest word for today.

Booking flights back home for the funeral, sorting logistics with Mom and figuring out how many days I can actually take off with Atlas still going. Practical mode, easier than feeling anything directly right now if I'm honest.

Awake again at four, this time it's not Atlas in my head, it's Nonna, just fragments, her voice, the smell of her kitchen, over and over. Grief and exhaustion tangled together into something I don't have a name for. Going to try to just lie here until the alarm rather than fight it.

Funeral was today. Strange how much logistics there are around grief, the seating, the programs, cousins I haven't seen in years all standing around in dark clothes making small talk about flights and traffic like it's any other family gathering. Most of the day I felt oddly outside myself, watching it happen rather than being in it. But there was one moment that broke through all of that, my cousin Elena told a story about Nonna chasing a raccoon out of her garden with a broom, shouting at it in Italian, and the whole room actually laughed, real laughing, and for just a second it didn't feel like a funeral at all, it felt like Nonna was still somehow in the room making everyone laugh the way she always did. I don't know how to hold both things at once, the sadness and that one bright second, but I think that's just what this is now.

Valentine's Day, muted this year for obvious reasons, but Sam was really kind about it, no big performance, just came over with soup and sat with me while I didn't talk much. Sometimes the best thing someone can do is just be present without needing you to be okay. Grateful for that tonight.

Home again from the trip, back in my own apartment, and the grief hit differently today, quieter but somehow heavier, in this completely mundane moment, just standing at the stove reheating leftovers and suddenly it was like a wave coming out of nowhere, having to just stand there and let it pass. Nobody around to see it, which was its own kind of hard. I think this is just how it's going to be for a while, ordinary moments turning into something else without warning.
Overcast Monday, the sky matching everything else lately. Went to work anyway, needed something to do with my hands and my hours. Flat day, nothing bad, just gray straight through.

Had lunch with Maya today and actually laughed, real laughing, at some ridiculous story she told about her coworker. Felt good for those minutes, genuinely good, and then almost immediately after felt strange about feeling good, like I wasn't supposed to be laughing this soon, like it meant something bad about how much I actually cared. I know that's not fair to myself, grief doesn't work on a schedule where you're not allowed to have a good hour here and there, but knowing it and feeling it are different things again, same as always.

Four a.m. again, tried reading to reset but the words weren't landing, just staring at the same paragraph for ten minutes. Grief and Atlas both circling tonight, taking turns. Going to try to just breathe through it until the alarm.

Pottery Thursday, and honestly it was the best hour of the week so far, hands busy with the clay means my head goes quiet in a way it doesn't otherwise right now. Made something almost decent, a little mug with a slightly crooked handle, but I don't even care that it's crooked. Grateful for this class more than I expected to be when I signed up back in January.

Grief has a way of ambushing you in grocery stores apparently. Was walking down the pasta aisle and saw San Marzano tomatoes, the exact brand Nonna always used for her sauce, and just stood there for a full minute holding the can like it might tell me something. Had to leave my cart for a second and just stand by the wall breathing. Nobody noticed, or if they did, nobody said anything, which I was grateful for. Bought the tomatoes anyway. Might try to make her sauce this weekend, badly probably, but I want to try.

Sam's been so steady through all of this, no pressure to be okay, no awkwardness around the grief stuff, just consistently present. Told them tonight how much that's meant, actually said it out loud instead of just feeling it privately. Grateful, genuinely, for having someone like that in my corner right now.

Sunday run, cold air biting but clear, and for the first time in a couple weeks it felt like something other than grief and exhaustion, just running, just cold air and legs moving. Small easing. Not gone, nothing like gone, but a little lighter today than most days lately.

Overcast Monday, back to the flat gray. Work fine, nothing remarkable, just moving through the week's motions. Still thinking about Nonna often, but it's settling into something quieter, a presence rather than a wound, most of the time anyway.

Atlas grinding on still, feels endless at this point, though the end is theoretically in sight in the next few weeks. Tired, just generally tired, work-tired layered over the other kind. Ordinary Tuesday otherwise.

Dinner with Maya and Tom, first time the three of us have hung out together in a while with everyone's schedules being what they are. Good to just be around people who've known me a long time, no explaining needed about anything, they just get where I'm at right now without me having to spell it out.

Made a bowl tonight in pottery that's actually, genuinely good. Not good for a beginner, just good, even, centered, the glaze test tile I picked for it should come out a deep blue. The instructor held it up to the rest of the class as an example of what patience with the wheel gets you, which was equal parts mortifying and kind of thrilling. I had this quiet thought while I was smoothing the rim that Nonna would have liked it, would have wanted to put fruit in it or something on her table, that specific kind of love where she'd use a thing you made instead of just admiring it from a shelf. Small joy tonight, sitting right next to the grief instead of replacing it. I think that's just how this works now.

Friday exhale, week survived, which after everything this month has felt like enough of a bar to clear. Ordered food, watched something mindless, didn't push myself toward anything productive. Sometimes just getting through counts.

Month's over, and it was a lot, more than a lot honestly. Losing Nonna, the funeral, Atlas somehow still going the whole time underneath it. Short entry tonight, just marking that February happened and I made it through. Onward to March I guess.
